title: Trio Sonata in G major, Op. 16 No. 1, WK 98
note: Work, WK 98, Op. 16 and recording (La Stagione, CPO/Classic Produktion, 9.5 min) are fine. But the bass is not shown to be an obbligato cello: the 1785 print says 'two for two flutes and a bass', CPO and Grove/Wikipedia say 2 flutes and basso continuo, IMSLP says 'cello (or continuo)'. If it is continuo the scoring should be {flute:2, continuo:1} and there is no string part (out of scope). Same question for sibling 102529 (WK 101).

title: Quintet in B-flat major
note: Recorded (CPO 19:44; Harnoncourt DAW 50 14:33, movement timings differ a lot). Is the theorbo/cello pair separate parts or the continuo group beside a concertante keyboard (owner rule: fold into continuo when unsure)? No score source found; may be 4 players.

title: Sonata a 2, Op. 8 No. 4 ("L'Obizza")
note: Exists and recorded (Clematis 4:00; Mvsica Perdvta, Brilliant, 5:34). Brilliant booklet: Sonata a 2 'L'Obizza' for violin, bass violin and b.c., so the scoring holds, but the 'or bassoon' alternative seems copied from La Galini (No. 15); IMSLP lists L'Obizza as 2 violins, viola. Alternative unconfirmed.

title: Trio Sonata in C major, Op. 1 No. 9
note: Recorded three times (7:37-7:55, 4 movements, 1704). Doubt on scoring only: IMSLP says the cello line of Nos. 7-8 is distinct from the continuo bass 'less so with no. 9'; if it mostly doubles the bass, the brief's rule (fold into continuo when unsure) would make it 2 violins + continuo, 3 players
